name: Sagunto
title: Sagunto Ship UTM | LNG, Car Carrier & Steel Ship Gauging
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement at Sagunto for LNG carriers, vehicle carriers and steel ships: ballast tank, deck and hold gauging at the open-coast terminals.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for LNG and Vehicle Carriers at Sagunto
intro: Sagunto is the northern port of the Valencia system, built on an open stretch of Mediterranean coast for gas, vehicles and heavy cargo. Its breakwater berths take LNG carriers, car carriers, steel ships and ro-ro vessels that need space and water the older city port lacks. Atlantis NDT sends a technician team from India to the ship at Sagunto, with gauging planned around the terminal's rules and the sea state.

highlights.p: Gas carriers at the regasification terminal work under strict gas-safety rules. Within the permit, we gauge ballast tanks, hull structure outside containment, deck supports and accessible machinery-space piping.
Car carriers load vehicles for export at the port's vehicle berths. Between discharge and loading, deck plating, ramps and ballast tanks can be measured, with crack detection at deck supports.
Sagunto's berths face open water, so swell and wind decide the working window. We agree a fallback day with the superintendent and avoid committing a team to a date the forecast does not support.

port.h: An open-coast port north of Valencia
p: Puerto de Sagunto lies a short distance north of the city of Valencia, on a flat coastal plain beside the old industrial town of Sagunto. Unlike the sheltered inner harbour of Valencia, it was built behind breakwaters on an exposed coast, with deeper water and more space for terminals. It belongs to the same port authority as Valencia and Gandia, but its character is different: energy, vehicles, steel and bulk rather than the container mass of the main port.

The anchor tenant is the LNG regasification terminal, where gas carriers discharge for the Spanish grid and, in some periods, for reloading. The port also has a large vehicle terminal that exports cars built in eastern Spain, berths for steel and metal products linked to the local steelworks tradition, and quays for dry bulk, ceramic raw materials and project cargo. Ro-ro and general cargo ships call regularly. Compared with the main port, there is less container traffic and a larger share of ships that need long, deep, uncrowded berths.

The sea is the main constraint. Easterly and south-easterly swell enters the port mouth in autumn and winter, which can interrupt berthing and make launch work at the anchorage unsafe, while summer is generally calm. Strong levante winds raise a swell that shipping agents watch closely. Ships waiting for a berth anchor off the coast, in open roads, and for that reason anchorage gauging at Sagunto is occasional rather than routine. Most work is planned at the berths, when discharge has finished and the weather holds.

facilities.h: Terminal berths, the gas jetty and the docking question
p: The LNG terminal sits within a tightly controlled safety zone, and any contractor needs prior clearance from the terminal operator as well as the master. The team keeps to spaces outside the cargo containment: ballast tanks, double-bottom and wing spaces reached from the ballast side, deck structure away from hazardous zones, and machinery-space piping. Vehicle carriers use their own berths, where discharge and loading are scheduled tightly, so the useful window may be only a few hours with the decks cleared.

Sagunto does not have a repair drydock for merchant ships. Vessels that need docking go to Valencia's own repair yard, a short coastal run to the south, or to yards elsewhere in Spain and the Mediterranean, and Sagunto readings are recorded so that the docking yard and the class surveyor can use them. Steel and bulk ships at the quays offer more time, because discharge takes days, and hold gauging can follow the cargo out once the terminal allows access.
list: LNG regasification terminal berth: ballast tank, hull and deck gauging on gas carriers outside containment, within terminal permits.
Vehicle terminal berths: car-deck, ramp and ballast tank gauging on car carriers between discharge and loading.
Steel and metal products quays: hold, hatch cover and tank top gauging on steel carriers after discharge.
Dry bulk and project cargo berths: hold frame and ballast tank readings on bulk and general cargo ships.
Open-roads anchorage: occasional launch-served gauging, only when swell and wind allow safe transfer.
Handover to a docking yard: readings in TM plan format for repair work in Valencia or elsewhere.

context.h: Spanish maritime authority and a changing gas trade
p: Spanish ports apply Paris MoU port state control through the maritime administration, with the local harbour master's office, the capitanía marítima, supervising ship operations and safety. Ships calling at Sagunto may be selected for inspection like those in any Spanish port, and the terminals add their own vetting for gas carriers and vehicle carriers. For a technician team the practical consequence is a permit regime that is strict, formal and carefully documented.

The ships at Sagunto sit in a fast-moving part of the market. LNG carriers are among the most valuable vessels afloat, and older steam-turbine ships are being retired or repurposed, so owners and buyers want solid evidence of hull condition. Vehicle carriers on European routes are subject to EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime accounting, and the Ship Recycling Regulation's Inventory of Hazardous Materials matters when an older vessel changes hands. Thickness readings taken at Sagunto help all of these decisions.

jobs.p: Work at Sagunto is planned around terminal rules and the forecast. The superintendent usually sends the TM plan and the ship's schedule, the terminal confirms the permitted spaces, and the team arrives once the berth is secured. Reports are returned in class-style format for survey planning or for a buyer's due diligence. Typical requests are: Where the ship will dock at Valencia afterwards, the same crew can travel south and continue in the yard, with equipment and permits arranged beforehand.
list: An LNG carrier at the terminal: ballast tank and double-bottom gauging from the ballast side, plus deck structure checks, ahead of a docking.
A car carrier between discharge and loading: lower-hold and fixed deck plating gauging, with magnetic particle testing at ramp hinges.
A steel carrier after discharge: hold frames, tank top and hatch cover gauging before the next steel cargo.
A ro-ro ship at the vehicle berth: deck, ramp and ballast tank readings during a scheduled lay-over.
Pre-purchase gauging of a gas or vehicle carrier alongside, supporting a buyer's technical inspection.

logistics: Valencia Airport is the main arrival point, with a road transfer north to Sagunto that is short compared with most port journeys, and Alicante and Barcelona are alternatives. Technicians from India need a Schengen visa for Spain, which we apply for once the call is confirmed. Terminal access, ISPS clearance and gas-terminal induction are arranged through the ship's agent, who submits the team's passport details and certificates ahead of time.

faqs.q: What can you gauge on an LNG carrier at the Sagunto terminal?
faqs.a: Spaces outside the cargo containment, within the terminal's and ship's permit: ballast tanks, wing and double-bottom spaces, deck structure away from hazardous zones and machinery-space piping. Cargo system work is left for a dry dock, and equipment must be accepted by the terminal.

faqs.q: Is there a dry dock at Sagunto?
faqs.a: No repair drydock for merchant ships. Ships that need docking usually go to the repair yard at Valencia or to other Spanish or Mediterranean yards. We prepare the Sagunto readings so any yard and class surveyor can use them for steel and survey planning.

faqs.q: Does swell prevent gauging at Sagunto?
faqs.a: It can affect berthing and anchorage transfers, particularly in autumn and winter with easterly swell. Work inside holds and tanks at a berth is less affected. We agree a fallback date with the superintendent and rely on the agent's forecast.

faqs.q: How long is a typical car carrier call?
faqs.a: Short, often under a day, with the useful window between discharge and loading. A focused scope on decks, ramps and a few ballast tanks fits that period. We agree the priority list in advance and measure the most important areas first.

faqs.q: Can hold gauging be done on bulk or steel ships while they discharge?
faqs.a: Only in holds that are already empty, swept and released by the terminal. Discharge at the steel and bulk quays can take days, so later holds often become free while earlier ones are still working. We agree the order with the agent and measure each hold as it is cleared, rather than waiting for the whole ship.
